title: Shadow minister Helen Goodman MP shows an interest
author: Ian Anstice / The Library Campaign

editorial.text: The last post reported on Ed Vaizey’s appearance and talk about public libraries at a Society of Chief Librarians’ event. The main news from this post is that his opposite number, Helen Goodman MP, is starting to take an interest as well. The Labour shadow minister’s statements are hardly showing revolutionary fervour – she’s OK with volunteers, for instance, running small branches as long as there’s paid qualified staff elsewhere – but they do show an awareness by someone on her team of what is going on. I suspect if you parse carefully what she says then there’s not that much difference between her and Ed, who has always been careful not to disparage paid staff, but there’s a difference in emphasis – she’s coming across as more keen on standards (to avoid a “postcode lottery”) for instance. Helen has started a brief enquiry into public libraries (there’s lots of those going on at the moment isn’t there?) and it will be interesting to see what the results are. I hope that whatever they are, they’re far more different to her opposite number than what we’ve seen so far. The general election is next year by the way.
